notes:
I couldn't write these notes because my research tool stopped working. My very first attempt to load the commentary pages failed with the message "no more code_execution tool calls remaining this turn," and a second try failed the same way. Searching and loading web pages only works through that tool, and my other tools have no internet access.

So I didn't read any pages: not Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary, Wesley's notes or any of the Catholic, Orthodox or scholarly sites. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Without the pages, I can't honestly write any verse note.

Here's what I'd do when we try again in a new turn or conversation:

1. **The traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word's Isaiah 5 page, Precept Austin's Isaiah 5 commentary, and Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on BibleHub and StudyLight.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Verse 4 ("What more could I have done…?") is the likeliest place. It comes up in arguments about whether God's grace can be resisted. I'd compare Wesley's notes (Methodist) with Gill (Baptist) and Reformed teachers on Monergism and Ligonier, plus Lutheran sources on lcms.org and 1517.org if they discuss it.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship (for example, the "Song of the Vineyard" and the Hebrew wordplay in v. 7). I'd also check how verses 1–7 connect to Jesus' parable of the tenants. For Catholic and Orthodox readings I'd search the Church Fathers and the Summa on newadvent.org, plus catholic.com and oca.org. For verse 20 I'd look at GotQuestions and Desiring God. I'd only cover prosperity, word-of-faith or hyper-grace teaching if a page on your list actually discusses this chapter.

If you'd like, ask again and I'll start with those sources.
